description:
Restless Mind | Slow Veena | 1.5 Hours of Rest

Still wired at the end of the day? Body's done but brain hasn't got the message yet — that's adrenaline still running. Slow Veena works directly on that. Not meditation, not sleep music. Just a sustained low-frequency sound that gives your nervous system something to follow down.

90 minutes of slow Veena in Raga Yaman — the classical evening raga — with a quiet Theta wave underneath to ease the mind from alert into rest.

🎵 What you'll hear:
- Veena — one of the oldest Indian instruments, deep and resonant in the low register
- Raga Yaman — the classical evening raga, designed to ease the transition from day to night
- A quiet Theta wave layer to guide the brain from alert into rest
- No percussion, no sudden changes — slow sustained phrases with long silences

⏱ Chapters
0:00   Still running
15:00  Starting to ease
35:00  Coming down
60:00  Settled
80:00  At rest

🧠 How to use:
Put it on when the day is done but your mind hasn't caught up. Sit, lie down, or just let it run in the background. Don't try to force calm — let the Veena set the pace.

⏱ Best for:
• Still wired after a long day
• Adrenaline that won't switch off
• Restless mind at night
• Coming down from a stressful day
• Background for evening wind-down

📺 Subscribe to Raga Focus for daily uploads:
- Sitar, Sarangi, Veena, Surbahar, Bansuri, Sarod and other Indian instruments
- Music for anxiety, overthinking, sleep, stress, emotional release

Central figure: serene woman in deep burgundy-and-gold sari seated cross-legged playing veena (recognisable as a large long-necked plucked instrument resting across the lap with a gourd resonator) in a quiet candlelit room, eyes half-closed, expression of settling calm. Single oil lamp nearby, warm amber light. Bold dark-teal serif overlay text reading 'EASE DOWN' centered, traditional Devanagari-influenced serif typography, high contrast for mobile readability. Deep amber-burgundy-cream palette, coming-down mood, single composed scene, no clutter.
suno_prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals. Slow veena solo in raga Yaman, late evening mood, deep resonant plucked notes with long sustain, no percussion, no tabla, 432Hz tuning, 55-65 BPM very slow tempo, sparse melodic phrases with long natural silences between them, low-mid register (warm and grounding, not sharp), cinematic evening production, settling and easing, suitable for extended looping. Raga Yaman tonic C or D. Emotionally: like the moment adrenaline finally stops — not sleepy yet, just beginning to come down. Warm, grounding, patient. Theta wave layer at -20dB underneath, very subtle.

production_spec.loop_seam: 10s in / 30s out, Suno extend 3-4x → loop in post to fill 90 min
production_spec.notes: Raga Yaman — classical evening raga, Kalyan thaat. Deep resonant veena low-mid register, NOT high-pitched. Theta 6Hz for transition from alert to rest (not deep sleep — Theta is the bridge state). LUFS -15 (evening audience, slightly louder than sleep content). EMOTIONAL TAG ROTATION: clip 1: 'easing down, like adrenaline finally switching off' · clip 2: 'warm and settling, like the end of a long exhale' · clip 3: 'patient and grounding, like sitting with the quiet'. CLINICAL HIT: Veena recovering tier — audio quality is critical here. First Suno clip must feel genuinely settling. If it feels too bright or too alert — regenerate.
